newsitem.title: JORDAN: FBI director in Jordan for talks.
newsitem.headline: FBI director in Jordan for talks.

text.p: U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) director Louis Freeh arrived in Jordan from Israel on Thursday and held talks with Jordanian officials, the United States embassy in Amman said.

An embassy spokesman declined to say who Freeh was meeting during his brief stay, or whether he would discuss Jordanian efforts to secure the release of Mousa Abu Marzook, a leading member of the Palestinian Islamic resistance group Hamas who is in a New York prison facing deportation to Israel.

Israeli security sources have said Israeli officials, fearing violent protests if Abu Marzook ended up in an Israeli jail, were examining a deal with U.S. and Jordanian officials to send him to Jordan in return for a pledge to shun violence.
Jordan's Justice Minister Abdul-Karim al-Dughmi said last week Freeh's delegation would hold "detailed talks" on the case of Abu Marzook.

The U.S. embassy said Freeh was in the Middle East to open FBI attache offices in Israel and Egypt, and was coming to Jordan "in response to an invitation extended by law enforcement officials of Jordan".
